channel.description: Recent content in The Marketing Lab on Marketing Sumo

item.title: Want a Sales Meeting? Stop Asking for One.
item.description: There’s an old saying in the startup world: ask for money, you get advice. Ask for advice, you get money. I think the same applies to B2B sales.

item.title: Stop Being the Bigger Person. Your Buyers Are Comparing You Anyway.
item.description: One piece of marketing advice refuses to die: “Never talk about your competitors.” The logic is simple. Don’t give them free publicity. Take the high road. Focus on your own strengths.

item.title: Nobody Wants to Read Your Customer Success Story
item.description: I have yet to meet a B2B marketer who proudly tells me, “Our case studies are our biggest source of leads.” Most companies have them. Very few buyers read them.

item.title: Your Event Didn't Fail. Your Marketing Did.
8 Tiny B2B Website Changes That Increase Conversion (That Most Companies Ignore)
item.description: Most B2B websites are still built like brochures. Hero statement. Features. Logos. Case studies. Contact form. The visitor does all the work. They read a paragraph, imagine the product, imagine the outcome, then imagine whether any of it applies to them.

item.title: Why Every B2B Company Should Have a Podcast
item.description: Most B2B companies are still trying to win attention in the worst possible way: cold emails, LinkedIn DMs, “quick 15-min demo?” requests. But here’s what’s actually happening on the other side.

item.title: Why B2B Tech Companies Suddenly Became Funny
item.description: Welcome to the first issue of The Marketing Lab. This newsletter exists because marketing changes faster than most playbooks do. Every issue, I’ll break down experiments, campaigns, trends, and ideas that are actually moving the needle and separate them from the recycled advice that somehow survives every algorithm update.
